description: An authenticated user can delete vet clinics belonging to other users by supplying an arbitrary vetId to POST /yourpets/vet/remove. The deleteVet endpoint accepts only vetId and encryptedMarketplaceId — it never checks that the requesting customer owns the vet record, so any user who knows or guesses a valid vetId can delete another user's vet clinic.

code_evidence.description: Deletes vet by vetId and encryptedMarketplaceId without verifying that the requesting customer owns the vet record. No customerId parameter exists; any caller with a valid vetId can delete it.
Controller delegates to VetBusinessLogic.deleteVet with only vetId and encryptedMarketplaceId. No customerId is accepted or forwarded for ownership validation.
Interface definition for DELETE /marketplaces/{encryptedMarketplaceId}/vets/{vetId} accepts only path params — no customerId header param for ownership verification.
Calls petsProfileService.removeVetClinic(vetId, encryptedMarketplaceId) without passing the authenticated customer's ID, so the backend has no way to enforce ownership.
Calls vetsResource.deleteVet(vetId, encryptedMarketplaceId) without customerId. The service-layer proxy omits any ownership context.

preconditions: Authenticated as any Amazon customer (user A)
A vet clinic record exists belonging to a different customer (user B)
Attacker knows or can enumerate the target vetId

reproduction_steps: Log in to amazon.com as user A.
Click 'Remove this vet clinic' on one of user A's own clinics.
Intercept the POST /yourpets/vet/remove request with a proxy.
Replace the vetId parameter value with a vetId belonging to user B.
Observe the response: {"success":true,"result":"VET CLINIC REMOVED SUCCESSFULLY","message":null}.
Verify that user B's vet clinic has been deleted (status set to INACTIVE).
exploit_evidence.expected_secure_behavior: The server should verify that the authenticated customer owns the vet record identified by vetId and return 401 Unauthorized if the customer IDs do not match.
exploit_evidence.observed_vulnerable_behavior: The server deletes the vet clinic identified by vetId regardless of which customer is making the request, returning a success response.
exploit_evidence.impact: Any authenticated Amazon customer can delete any other customer's vet clinic records by manipulating the vetId parameter. This is a data-destructive IDOR affecting all users of the Pets Profile vet clinics feature.

fix_evidence.fix_description: Three-part fix: (1) CR-155175404 adds a customerId header param to the PetsProfileServiceInterface deleteVet definition and adds ownership validation in VetBusinessLogic.deleteVet — if customerId is provided and does not match the vet record's customerId, a 401 NotAuthorizedException is thrown. (2) CR-155679540 updates PetsProfileWebsite to pass the authenticated customer's ID when calling removeVetClinic. (3) CR-155869672 makes customerId a required field in VetsController.deleteVet, throwing BadRequestException if it is missing.
